newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka says to privatise four more estate firms.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka says to privatise four more estate firms.

text.p: Sri Lanka plans to privatise four more plantation firms in July by selling strategic holdings to investors on the Colombo Stock Exchange, a senior government official said on Thursday.

"We will sell 51 percent or strategic holdings in four more estate firms, starting from July 4 onwards," said an official of the Public Enterprise Reform Commission (PERC), who declined to be identified.
Malwatte Plantations Ltd will be sold on July 4, followed by Kahawatte Plantations Ltd on July 7, Elpitiya Plantations Ltd on July 8 and Elkaduwa Plantations Ltd a day later, he said.
Malwatte Plantations will be introduced for sale at a minimum price of 40 rupees for a ten-rupee share. The balance three will be introduced at a minimum price of 30 rupees a share.

"Six bidders have submitted proposals to take part in bidding for the four firms. The names of those shortlisted will be made public on Monday," said the official from PERC, the state body which oversees privatisations.
The shortlisted parties will be entitled to bid for either one or all the firms, he said.
Sri Lanka began privatising 23 plantation firms which own some 600,000 hectares of tea, rubber and coconut lands in 1992.
Management was privatised in 1992 and broadened to include ownership in 1995.

The process, which involves selling 51 percent or 10.2 million shares to a strategic investor, gifting 10 perent to employees and selling all but one share to the public, has been completed in six plantation firms, which now comprise the plantation sector on the Colombo Stock Exchange.
The government retains one "golden" share in all the firms, which empowers it to intervene in case of mismanagement.
Strategic holdings have already been sold in nine firms with the initial public offers due later in the year, the PERC official said.
"We still have four firms where nothing has been done as yet," he said.
